description: Functional refactoring suggestions (light bulb quick fixes) for F#, built on FSharp.Analyzers.SDK. Over 130 rules covering correctness, performance, idiom and redundancy; every one is Hint severity, so they never gate a build.
releaseNotes: 0.7.4: fixes from sweeping SQLProvider, which the tool left with a broken build. FR0140 parenthesises the value it moves into a construction: a cast binds looser than the named property, so cmd.Connection then con cast to SqlConnection folded to an equality against an undefined Connection. The all-frameworks arbiter now counts errors both ways rather than asking pass or fail - a project can be broken for two reasons at once, and a pre-existing breakage outside the snapshot made every fix look innocent and put them all back. The generated-file sniff reads thirty lines and knows the prose and attribute forms, not just the XML marker, so a FAKE-written AssemblyInfo is left alone. The Visual Studio extension checks the file rather than trusting the buffer content type: F# sources only, and never a vendored, package or generated path. --parse-only no longer reads framework-conditional DefineConstants, which activated one framework branch and hid the rest. FR0039 pairs with the project own framework guard like FR0038 does, so a StringComparison overload no longer breaks netstandard2.0; FR0119 keeps its advice but withholds the edit where a guard would be needed, its rewrite spanning more than one edit. 0.7.3: FR0141 stays silent inside async and task, where the advice does not hold: a task compiles to a resumable state machine and recursive return! grows the stack, and in async the recursive function must return an Async so the change reaches the signature rather than the loop. FR0141 notes a while loop that carries state forward by mutation and leaves through a boolean flag - tail recursion written inside out. Deliberately not the search loop: a carried value whose every assignment is a counter bump is an index, and that shape already short-circuits and allocates nothing (measured 12x faster than Array.exists on an early hit). Note only. FR0107 documented accurately: it already folds a pure let-prefix into the lambda, which the rule text denied. 140 rules. FR0140 folds property assignments that immediately follow a construction into F#'s named-property construction - not a constructor overload and not faster, the same calls in the same order, but the object reads as constructed rather than assembled and the half-built value stops being nameable. Only the uninterrupted run straight after the binding folds in. 139 rules. FR0089 no longer reads the F# 6 indexer spelling as a single-tuple list. Since F# 6, grid[0, 1, 2] parses as an ATOMIC application of a bracket to the thing before it, the same shape as the [ 1, 2 ] paste trap the rule hunts, so every multi-dimensional index raised a false correctness note. The atomic flag is what separates them, and a spaced list argument stays flagged. Found by surveying an agent-generated corpus, where all six of the rule notes in one test file were this and none a real trap. Both index spellings are now locked into the tests across the rule set: every rule that DETECTS indexing already matched the atomic form beside the legacy DotIndexedGet node, and the rest only traverse into brackets. SARIF reports now name the URL the package and --help publish. 0.7.2: FR0139 swaps Seq functions to the Array module where the typed tree proves an array — measured on .NET 10, arrays only, with `contains` on int arrays defaulting to vectorised Enumerable.Contains and offering Array.contains beside it. Rule fixes found by dogfooding and by re-sweeping the corpus: FR0030 no longer emits code that cannot parse for a range source, FR0119 binds only on a computation expression's own statement spine (21 rollbacks in one repo), FR0029 tail extraction stops at a `use` and FR0005 cures the shape an older version wrote, FR0039 keeps backticked receivers, and a failed verification no longer leaves kept fixes suppressed. The benchmarks now target .NET 10. 0.7.1: the published package now reliably carries BOTH analyzer SDK builds flat in analyzers/dotnet/fs — FSharp.Refactor.Analyzers.Ionide.dll for stock Ionide (SDK 0.35.0) and the 0.37.2 build for the CLI and newer FsAutoComplete — plus the review-hardening fixes 0.7.0's rolling pack accumulated; the repository gains a classic Visual Studio extension (VSIX): squiggles and light-bulb fixes in VS 2022-2026 rendered from an FsAutoComplete sidecar. 0.7.0: cross-file migrations arrive — under --api-changes, strictly internal declarations now migrate project-wide with every use classified against its own file (FR0069 voption, FR0093 struct tuples, FR0049 taskify), gated hard: public never, InternalsVisibleTo assemblies never, one unconvertible use vetoes everything. FR0029 grows branch-return tail extraction and per-arm match/match! splitting into nested tasks, and match! arm interiors are finally visible to every rule (an SDK walker hole). Solution runs order narrowest target first and shared directive-free files sweep once across all frameworks and projects; fully-swept compilations skip their typecheck. New rules: FR0132 trailing comments promote to XML docs; FR0133 five-word test names become double-backtick sentences (locals opt-in); FR0134 UtcNow-fed DateTime fields migrate to DateTimeOffset (opt-in); FR0135 markdown-bearing script comments become literate (** cells. FR0022 also mines field names from XAndY case names and clear trailing comments. Everything adversarially audited: keyword field names, fake-clock shadowing, cross-type comparisons, multi-line plain strings under re-indentation, TestCaseSource string references and more are all vetoed by construction. FR0136 states zero-argument Guid constructors as Guid.Empty (the editor also offers NewGuid()); FR0137 fuses consecutive same-module map passes via composition; FR0035 gains the module-level-set quick-fix (in-place Set.ofList when probes are the only uses, a HashSet companion otherwise); FR0039 extends its fix to the method-call shape (path.ToLower().StartsWith "file:" becomes the StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase overload, per the .NET string best-practices guide); FR0005 collapses no-op return! task wrappers and unjustified tail thunks; the multi-pass loop warns on non-convergence and blocks a rule that keeps growing the same file, and a failed verification now rolls back only the fixes at the error sites instead of every fix in the file. FR0138 rewrites hand-rolled emptiness tests (isNull x || x = "") to String.IsNullOrEmpty/IsNullOrWhiteSpace; FR0139 swaps Seq functions to the Array module where the typed tree proves an array (measured 2.3x on exists, enumerator allocation gone) - arrays only, and never the numeric aggregates that FR0041 sends to vectorised LINQ. 138 rules. 0.6.8: fixes first — a run now prints its fixes and holds advisory notes to one summary line (--notes lists them, --report exports SARIF). FR0029 applies its own FS3511 advice: hoisting pre-await lets (documenting comments travel along), splitting branching tasks per arm, wrapping non-awaiting tails, extracting awaiting try/finally suffixes; the multi-pass loop chains the moves. FR0049 rewrites blocking binds (GetAwaiter().GetResult(), .Result, Async.RunSynchronously) to let!/do! in task and async alike; sync-direction swaps stay config-opt-in. Suppression policy (suppressions: all/no-correctness/none plus --honor-suppressions) and per-rule config parameters. New rules FR0117-FR0131: or-pattern arm folding; CancellationToken omission and None-propagation; awaitable-twin calls; catch blocks logging without the exception (PII-aware); DateTime.Now/UtcNow.Date pitfalls; invalid regexes; Monitor.Enter/Exit to lock; interpolated logging to message templates; invisible/bidi Unicode with escape fixes; process-execution sinks; provider-format API-key literals; obsolete crypto constructors to static factories; guard-equality clauses to literal patterns; module constants gain [<Literal>]; provably tail-recursive functions gain [<TailCall>]. match/match!/function parity for arm rules; SHA1 editor alternatives on FR0065. 130 rules.
